variants.text: Hobson records that in the first half of the eighteenth century decorators in Holland, Germany and elsewhere enamelled whatever white porcelain they could obtain.
霍布森記載，十八世紀上半葉荷蘭、德國等地的彩繪匠人，凡能取得的白瓷都拿來加彩。

statements.originalText: Hobson notes that such added decoration was usually in Oriental taste and might be confused with indifferent Chinese work.

qualifiers.attribution: R. L. Hobson, Chinese Pottery and Porcelain (1915)

variants.text: Hobson notes that such added decoration was usually in Oriental taste and might be confused with indifferent Chinese work.
霍布森指出，這類後加彩多採東方趣味，可能與水準平平的中國作品相混。

statements.originalText: Hobson says such pieces can be recognised by the inferior quality of the enamels and the stiff drawing of the copyists.

qualifiers.attribution: R. L. Hobson, Chinese Pottery and Porcelain (1915)

variants.text: Hobson says such pieces can be recognised by the inferior quality of the enamels and the stiff drawing of the copyists.
霍布森說，這類器物可由較差的彩料品質與仿繪者僵硬的筆法辨識出來。

statements.originalText: Hobson lists the Chinese porcelains European enamellers favoured: slightly decorated pieces, plain white wares, wares with incised or carved design under the glaze, and white Fujian porcelain.

qualifiers.attribution: R. L. Hobson, Chinese Pottery and Porcelain (1915)

variants.text: Hobson lists the Chinese porcelains European enamellers favoured: slightly decorated pieces, plain white wares, wares with incised or carved design under the glaze, and white Fujian porcelain.
霍布森列舉歐洲彩繪匠人偏好的中國瓷器：紋飾簡少者、素白器、釉下刻劃花者及福建白瓷。

statements.originalText: Hobson notes that Chinese porcelain decorated in Europe with Oriental patterns has caused much perplexity to collectors.

qualifiers.attribution: R. L. Hobson, Chinese Pottery and Porcelain (1915)

variants.text: Hobson notes that Chinese porcelain decorated in Europe with Oriental patterns has caused much perplexity to collectors.
霍布森指出，在歐洲以東方紋樣加彩的中國瓷器曾令收藏家大感困惑。

statements.originalText: Hobson describes a Franks Collection box made from the lower part of a square vase that had been broken and cut down, and then fitted with a bronze cover in Japan.

qualifiers.attribution: R. L. Hobson, Chinese Pottery and Porcelain (1915)

variants.text: Hobson describes a Franks Collection box made from the lower part of a square vase that had been broken and cut down, and then fitted with a bronze cover in Japan.
霍布森描述弗蘭克斯收藏的一件盒，由破損方瓶的下部截短製成，之後在日本配上青銅蓋。

statements.originalText: The Jingdezhen taolu records that enamelled ware, little esteemed before, flourished from the early Qianlong reign, and that its workshops were commonly called 'red shops'.

variants.text: The Jingdezhen taolu records that enamelled ware, little esteemed before, flourished from the early Qianlong reign, and that its workshops were commonly called 'red shops'.
《景德鎮陶錄》記載，彩器先前不太受重視，自乾隆初年起逐漸興盛，其作坊俗稱「紅店」。

statements.originalText: Cleveland notes that some Qing imperial wares may have been sent undecorated from Jingdezhen to palace workshops in Beijing, where court painters applied the enamels.

qualifiers.attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art (object record)

variants.text: Cleveland notes that some Qing imperial wares may have been sent undecorated from Jingdezhen to palace workshops in Beijing, where court painters applied the enamels.
克利夫蘭美術館指出，部分清代官窯瓷器可能以未加彩飾的狀態由景德鎮運至北京宮廷作坊，再由宮廷畫師施加釉上彩。

statements.originalText: Cleveland lists the wine cup's earliest recorded owner as Men-Chu Wang of Beijing, with the note 'Probably Palace Collection'.

qualifiers.attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art (object record)

variants.text: Cleveland lists the wine cup's earliest recorded owner as Men-Chu Wang of Beijing, with the note 'Probably Palace Collection'.
克利夫蘭美術館著錄此酒杯最早的記錄藏家為北京 Men-Chu Wang，並註「可能為宮廷舊藏」。

statements.originalText: The Art Institute of Chicago records its teabowls as owned by Henry Charles Schwab of Chicago and bequeathed to the museum in 1941.

qualifiers.attribution: Art Institute of Chicago (object description, CC BY 4.0)

variants.text: The Art Institute of Chicago records its teabowls as owned by Henry Charles Schwab of Chicago and bequeathed to the museum in 1941.
芝加哥藝術博物館記其茶碗原為芝加哥 Henry Charles Schwab 所藏，1941年遺贈入館。

statements.originalText: The V&A traces its Chenghua stem cup through a Sotheby's sale of 11 May 1954, lot 17, back to a named owner and the Oliphant collection.

qualifiers.attribution: Victoria and Albert Museum (object record)

variants.text: The V&A traces its Chenghua stem cup through a Sotheby's sale of 11 May 1954, lot 17, back to a named owner and the Oliphant collection.
V&A 依1954年5月11日蘇富比拍賣第17號拍品，追溯其成化高足杯至具名前藏家及 Oliphant 收藏。

statements.originalText: Cleveland lists the cup's inclusion in the 1970–71 'Ming Porcelains' exhibition at China House Gallery, New York.

qualifiers.attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art (object record)

variants.text: Cleveland lists the cup's inclusion in the 1970–71 'Ming Porcelains' exhibition at China House Gallery, New York.
克利夫蘭美術館記此杯曾參加1970–71年紐約華美協進社（China House Gallery）「明代瓷器」展。

statements.originalText: Cleveland qualifies the palace provenance of its cup with the word 'Probably', so the record does not establish imperial custody.

qualifiers.attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art (object record)

variants.text: Cleveland qualifies the palace provenance of its cup with the word 'Probably', so the record does not establish imperial custody.
克利夫蘭美術館以「可能」一詞限定此杯的宮廷來源，因此該著錄並不確立其曾為宮廷收藏。

statements.originalText: Bushell warned that many 'marks' in Julien's book are of fictitious origin, so the book must be used with caution.

qualifiers.attribution: S. W. Bushell, Oriental Ceramic Art (1899)

variants.text: Bushell warned that many 'marks' in Julien's book are of fictitious origin, so the book must be used with caution.
卜士禮提醒，儒蓮（Julien）書中許多「款識」出處虛構，使用時須謹慎。

statements.originalText: Hobson cites one Chinese text while warning that it 'does not inspire confidence'.

qualifiers.attribution: R. L. Hobson, Chinese Pottery and Porcelain (1915)

variants.text: Hobson cites one Chinese text while warning that it 'does not inspire confidence'.
霍布森引用一部中文著作時提醒，該書「難以令人信賴」。

statements.originalText: Cleveland notes that a bowl carries a modern registration mark 'PDF A552' showing it was formerly in the Sir Percival David collection.

qualifiers.attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art (object record)

variants.text: Cleveland notes that a bowl carries a modern registration mark 'PDF A552' showing it was formerly in the Sir Percival David collection.
克利夫蘭美術館指出一件碗上有現代登錄記號「PDF A552」，表示其曾為大維德爵士（Percival David）收藏。

statements.originalText: Cleveland states that the labels on a plate's base testify that it was in the former Garland and Morgan collections.

qualifiers.attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art (object record)

variants.text: Cleveland states that the labels on a plate's base testify that it was in the former Garland and Morgan collections.
克利夫蘭美術館說明，一件盤底的標籤證明其曾為 Garland 與 Morgan 舊藏。

statements.originalText: Cleveland describes the storage-box lid of a late Ming bowl inscribed by Seifū Yohei III with his seal.

qualifiers.attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art (object record)

variants.text: Cleveland describes the storage-box lid of a late Ming bowl inscribed by Seifū Yohei III with his seal.
克利夫蘭美術館描述一件晚明碗的收納箱蓋上，有清風與平三代的題字及鈐印。

statements.originalText: Cleveland records a second box inscription in a different hand dating the bowl to the very end of the Ming dynasty.

qualifiers.attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art (object record)

variants.text: Cleveland records a second box inscription in a different hand dating the bowl to the very end of the Ming dynasty.
克利夫蘭美術館記載箱上另有他人筆跡的題記，將此碗定為明代末年之作。

statements.originalText: Cleveland notes that the Seifū studio members who wrote such inscriptions were not specialist examiners, though they knew imported Chinese wares.

qualifiers.attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art (object record)

variants.text: Cleveland notes that the Seifū studio members who wrote such inscriptions were not specialist examiners, though they knew imported Chinese wares.
克利夫蘭美術館指出，書寫此類題記的清風家成員並非專門的審定者，但熟悉輸入的中國器物。
